officialSourceChecks.observed: FTC says to research sellers, get return/refund policies in writing, look near the karat mark for the responsible company's name or U.S. registered trademark, and defines 'solid gold' as not hollow. It separately describes plated, filled, overlay/RGP and vermeil terms.

§23.18(a) states it is unfair or deceptive to misrepresent the weight of a diamond; subsections (b)–(d) discuss diamond carat/point and fractional diamond-weight representations. It does not set a ring-alloy gram-weight disclosure requirement.
eCFR identifies §23.10 as additional guidance for use of quality marks; the displayed current title was up to date as of 10/21/2026.

Official GovInfo U.S. Code text for §295 gives the gold fineness tolerances (3/1000 for the applicable solder-free test and 7/1000 for the entire quantity of other articles with solder), with scope described through the covered commerce in §§294–295.

Official GovInfo U.S. Code text for §297(b) describes an identifying trademark or name placed as close as possible to the quality mark/stamp, for manufacturers/dealers subject to §294. This is an official alternative to the Cornell mirror currently recorded in the canonical reference list.
Official NIST Appendix B.8 page fetched; project evidence records its rounded troy-ounce-to-gram factor and distinguishes it from Kitco's stated 31.1034768 g/ozt constant.

Official product page states '14ky, 4.7g, #B02561' and says to call (309) 452-1612 for current pricing and availability. The page does not state a payment method. Canonical seller data says 'Not stated; price is quoted by phone.'

FTC says consumers have legal rights and responsibilities, including the right to dispute billing errors; the page does not establish that every ring seller accepts cards or that any specific seller does not accept wire/Zelle/gift cards.
